en: The Glorious Eight Verses on Murukaḥ
I salute day and night the Lord Vighnarāja, the bestower of success and wisdom, the elder brother of Subrahmaṇyā, and the son of Soma’s daughter.
The letter *m* signifies Mukunda, while the letter *ru* denotes Rudra.
The letter 'ka' is the proclaimer of Brahman; Muruka is the designator of Guha.
O Lord Muruka, glorious one, supreme bestower of enjoyment and liberation!
O God of gods, O Great Being, protect me, protect me always, O All-pervading One!
O Lord Muruka, the God who grants liberation, the Master who brings joy to the sages!

We always offer salutations to the liberator from all sufferings, the destroyer of delusion. We are forever protected by Muruka, Mukunda— who dwells within the hearts of sages— the Lord of the Vine (Vallīśa), and the Great Lord (Maheśa).
Salutations to Muruka in the morning; salutations to Muruka at night;
salutations to Muruka in the evening; salutations, salutations to Muruka.
[6] From the supreme, true Muruka, the six-faced one who has the peacock as his vehicle.
I do not know anything else beyond Guha; he is always my reality.
I perpetually worship the feet of the Lord, the General of the Army of Creepers, the Great Lord of Muraka, the playful manifestation of the ether of consciousness.
May the mind always delight in the god Muruka, the six-faced one, whose vehicle is the peacock, who possesses twelve arms, the son of Kṛttikā, and the son of Śambhu.
For one who constantly recites this hymn of praise, there shall be eternal auspiciousness.
